topic: THE 1966-1970 TALISMANS ARE THE MISSING PORTRAIT BOOKS FOR THIS BLOCK, AND THEY ARE NOT ON archive.org

topic: NEW ASSET: THE 1966-1970 TALISMANS ARE NOW OCR'd, 990 PAGES
note: Built 5 September 2026 and kept at ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/_talisman-ocr-1966-1970/, one JSON per volume, about 2.8 MB. Every page of all eight PDFs, rendered at twice the scan's native pixel width and read with ocrmac (Apple Vision), stored as [{page, w, h, runs:[[text, confidence, [x,y,w,h] normalised]]}]. Quality is the difference between nothing and everything: the page that gives 'Cill. ,;.,~"' in the embedded layer gives 'Advisor: John Estill, Vice President; Karen Edmonds, President' from Vision. It runs at about one second a page, so the whole set rebuilds in twenty minutes on four workers. The bounding boxes are stored, so a name run can be turned straight into a crop rectangle. GREP THIS BEFORE RENDERING ANYTHING for 1966-1970.

topic: SCAN CEILING FOR 1966-1970: ONE SPREAD PER PAGE AT 1728 PIXELS
note: Every page of all eight PDFs is a single landscape image of a two-page spread, 1728 by 1152 pixels on a 1296 by 864 point page. That is 96 dpi, and it works out at about 864 by 1152 pixels for each printed page. It is the same ceiling recorded for the TopSCHOLAR Talismans of 1982-1991. A full-page studio portrait still cuts at around 480 by 630, which is good; a face in a class grid cuts at around 100 by 130, which is small but real; a face in a large group photograph is not worth cutting. Render with matrix zoom = native_image_width / page_width, then multiply by two for OCR only. Do not render at a fixed zoom.

topic: THE 1966-1970 VOLUMES CAPTION BY ROW, WHICH IS BETTER THAN THE 1970s ALPHABETICAL BLOCKS
note: From 1971 on, the Talisman class sections run alphabetical name blocks against a photograph grid and every identification is a counting argument. The 1966-1970 volumes do not. Their group photographs are captioned 'First Row: ... Second Row: ...' with the names enumerated in order, and their Who's Who and honours sections print a biographical block per person with that person's own portrait adjacent in the same column. Both are far more provable than a grid. Class section locations, by PDF page: tal1967-pt2 seniors 26-38, juniors 39-46, sophomores 47-57, freshmen 58-72. tal1968 seniors 126-139, juniors 140-150, sophomores 151-161, freshmen 162-178. tal1966 seniors 108-125. The 1969 and 1970 volumes hide their section headings from the embedded layer and have to be found through the new OCR index.

SETTLED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. The College Heights Herald did NOT run a People Poll, or any photographed-students opinion feature, in the 1960s or 1970s. Do not send another agent after it. TWO INDEPENDENT PROOFS. (1) INDEX. In the WKU Archives' own item-level index of the whole digitised run (local mirror data/herald-index-full.json, 11,850 items) the string 'People Poll' occurs 295 times and every single one falls in 1993-1998, plus a later revival in 2011 and 2013. First occurrence 1993-01-26, 'People Poll: What Do You Think of Marriott After Its First Semester Here?'. Zero before 1993. The index is NOT thinner for the 1960s-70s, which is the objection that would otherwise kill this: restricted to actual College Heights Herald issues, 1966-1979 carries 728 issues at 29.3 index lines each, and 1993-1998 carries 336 issues at 30.4 lines each. Only 0.3 per cent of the 1966-79 lines hit the 300-character truncation cap, so CLAUDE.md's warning about truncated abstracts does not bite on this era. POSITIVE CONTROL: rank the recurring standing features and the 1993-98 list reads 'just a second' 84, 'campus line' 84, 'for the record' 84, 'people poll' 84 - the indexer records a standing feature every time it runs. The same ranking for 1966-1979 gives 'what's happening' 229, 'ombudsman' 48, 'alumni news' 40, 'coming events calendar' 40, 'editorial cartoon' 31, 'hilltopics' 25, and NOTHING resembling a photo poll anywhere in the top 35. (2) NEWSPRINT. Four Opinion pages pulled and looked at, spread across the range: 2 Nov 1967 (47:10, p.4), 1 Feb 1972 (51:32, p.4), 2 Mar 1976 (51:45, p.4) and 3 Oct 1978 (54:12, p.4, the page headed 'Opinion' outright). All four are the identical furniture: one or two set editorials, one editorial cartoon, the staff masthead, and 'Letters to the editor'. No photograph of a student appears on any of them. The 1976 page adds an 'Ombudsman' question-and-answer column and an 'Aberrations' column, both unillustrated. The feature simply does not exist in this era.

topic: THE OPINION-PAGE TRAP IS REAL AND IT NAMES OUR OWN OFFICERS - VERIFIED ON THE PAGE
note: The brief warned that letter-signature blocks mimic poll labels in OCR. Confirmed on the actual newsprint, and it is worse than a generic warning: it fires on THIS BLOCK'S OFFICERS LIST. The Herald sets a letter writer's name in bold, then class rank and dorm underneath on their own short lines - 'Randi Jensen / Publicity chairman, Associated Students / Junior / State Hall' on the Opinion page of 2 Nov 1967. Randi Jensen is officer number 6 on _officers-n6679.json. She is NOT PICTURED on that page; there is no photograph of any student on it. The block is a signature, nothing more. The 1972 page does the same for Nat Ritter, Hank L. Miles, Tim Brownlee, John Campbell, Fred Tutor and Jackie Aeberoold, and the 1978 page for Robert Riley and Barbara Hayes. Any agent that greps Herald OCR for an officer surname, finds it in a bold short-line block, and cuts the nearest photograph will produce a confident, sourced, WRONG portrait. On Herald Opinion pages, a name in bold is a byline or a signature until a caption proves otherwise.

topic: LEAF OFFSET FOR THE 1979 TALISMAN IS MINUS ONE, NOT MINUS THREE
note: The brief and _talisman-index.json give leaf minus three for 1972, 1976 and 1977. That is NOT the 1979 offset. Checked three times against the printed folio on archive.org/details/talisman1979west: leaf n289 is printed p. 288, n290 is p. 289, n292 is p. 291. For 1979 the rule is leaf = printed page + 1. Anyone who applies minus three to a 1979 index page number lands two leaves early and will read the wrong caption onto a face. Fetch full-resolution single pages at archive.org/download/talisman1979west/page/nNNN.jpg - they come back at about 3082 by 4190, far better than the 1728-pixel TopSCHOLAR spreads, and are not rate limited.

topic: _talisman-index.json's 'likely_sga_page' FOR 1979 IS WRONG - IT IS 288-289, NOT 336
note: likely_sga_page lists 1979 as p. 336 with nine people on it. Page 336 was fetched and it is the FRATERNITIES section, the 'brother to brother' feature, carrying a Sigma Chi group photograph and SAE copy. The volume's real ASG section is printed pp. 288-289, which is what the back index says ('Associated Student Government 53, 73, 82, 119, 262, 288-9'). The nine-people count that produced 336 came from officer surnames colliding with fraternity copy. Both ASG pages were fetched and read. p. 288 carries three captioned photographs and they name only Steve Thornton twice and Victor Jackson once. p. 289 is the story 'Making news about entertainment' with two photographs, one of ASG newsletters on a floor and one of a meeting, neither naming a person in its caption. No 1978-79 officer other than Thornton is captioned anywhere in the ASG section.

topic: ALICE WICKS AND DAVID YOUNG ARE NOT PICTURED IN THE 1979 TALISMAN - CLOSED
note: Both checked against the volume's own back index, which is a full student directory and lists students who were never photographed. 'Wicks, Alice Elizabeth' appears with NO page number at all, immediately before 'Wicks, Joel David' who also has none. She is enrolled and indexed and appears on no page of the book. 'Young, David Paul' carries exactly one page, 289. Page 289 was fetched: he is named in the body text - the new constitution 'established 24 separate races for the 24 representative-at-large seats on ASG congress. David Young, administrative vice president, said this was done to force some heads-up competition' - and that text mention is what the index is pointing at. He is in no photograph and no caption on it. So the 1979 Talisman confirms David Young's office in words and gives no face for either of them. Do not re-fetch p. 289 expecting a portrait.

topic: STEVE WILSON IS PROBABLY TWO DIFFERENT MEN AND THE OFFICERS FILE HAS MERGED THEM
note: Flagging rather than fixing, per CLAUDE.md. _officers-n6679.json gives one Steve Wilson with 'Junior class representative at large (1971-72); Judicial Council Chairman (1978-79)'. Those two terms cannot belong to one undergraduate: a junior in 1971-72 graduates in 1973 and is six years gone by 1978-79. The 1979 Talisman back index makes it worse rather than better, because it carries TWO near-identical names - 'Wilson, Stephen Alan' with no pages and 'Wilson, Steve Alan 296, 318, 320, 336' - on top of 'Wilson, Stevie Joe 379'. Page 336 was fetched to test the Steve Alan entry and it is the fraternities feature; the body text there has a Steve Wilson coordinating Spring Sing for Sigma Alpha Epsilon and singing in their barbershop quartet, which is a fraternity man, not evidence of a judicial chairman. NO PORTRAIT SHOULD BE CUT FOR STEVE WILSON until the archive decides how many Steve Wilsons it is describing, because any face found is unassignable between them. This is a years.json question, not a photograph question.

topic: ALICE WICKS IS IN THE TALISMANS BUT ONLY EVER INSIDE A SIXTY-PERSON SORORITY GROUP - NOT CUTTABLE
note: Corrects the impression that she is simply absent. She is in the 1977 and 1978 volumes, and in both she is an Alpha Delta Pi in a very large outdoor group photograph, named by initial only. 1977 printed p. 263 (leaf n266), caption '(Second row) K. Kyser, A. Pickens, T. Price, C. Lanier, A. Wicks, B. Stafford ...', about seventy women. 1978 printed p. 334 (leaf n337), caption '(Third row) B. Myers, G. Moore, K. Maddoz, V. Bechtel, A. Wicks, J. Bertelson ...', sixty-two women in four captioned rows of 18, 17, 16 and 11. Position five from the left end of a row sounds countable and I fetched the 1978 frame at full resolution to try it. It is not. The women are banked up a slope in front of a brick building and the visual rows do not partition the way the caption's four rows do: heads from the second and third ranks interleave, and at the left end there is at least one head that could belong to either. Getting the rank wrong puts a stranger's face on an executive officer of ASG. NOT CUT, deliberately. She has no page reference at all in the 1979 or 1980 back indexes, so those two volumes never photographed her. If anyone revisits this, the way in is a Herald photograph of the 1978-79 secretary, not the Talisman.

topic: DAVE ROBERTS AND DAVID BASS: BOTH CLOSED, EACH FOR A DIFFERENT REASON
note: DAVE ROBERTS. The 1979 back index gives 'Roberts, David Norman 126, 338'. Both fetched. Printed p. 338 (leaf n339) is the fraternities feature and the only Roberts on it is 'D. Roberts' buried in the back row of a Sigma Nu group of about forty-eight men - an initial in a crowd, worth nothing. Printed p. 126 is a graduation feature whose body text runs 'Dave Roberts, an accounting major from Lexington, decided to give his parents a gradu-'; the caption beside it is about a different student, Pat Mountain. So the index's two pointers are one crowd and one text mention. He also carries 1977 p. 285 and 1978 pp. 326, 330, which were not fetched and are the only thing left to try. DAVID BASS. The existing _do-not-use.json ruling is CORRECT and I am confirming it rather than reopening it, having re-fetched the frame from archive.org at 3036 pixels rather than from the TopSCHOLAR spread. 1978 printed p. 34 (leaf n37) is the ASG page; the caption reads 'A LIGHT MOMENT IN AN ASG MEETING brings laughter from president Bob Moore and smiles from activities vice president David Bass, secretary Sharon May and vice president Cathy Murphy'. At full resolution the frame holds exactly four people: the laughing man in a white tank top, who is Moore because the caption says the laughter is his; a woman at the right with long dark hair; a foreground figure in sunglasses with feathered hair and a collared denim shirt whose sex genuinely cannot be read; and a fourth person at the bottom left turned away with no face at all. Bass is the sunglasses figure or the turned-away figure and nothing on the page says which. The 1978 back index gives him page 34 and nothing else, so this is the only frame that exists. Closed.

topic: WHERE THE 1978-79 CLASS PORTRAITS ARE NOT, AND THE ONE LEAD LEFT
note: Checked the printed class-grid name lists (the 'SURNAME, hometown' runs) across the 1976, 1977, 1978 and 1979 full texts on archive.org for all four of the 1978-79 officers. There is NO class portrait entry for Alice Wicks, David Young or David Roberts in any of the four. There is one for Wilson: 'STEVE A. WILSON, Bowling Green' appears in the 1976, 1977 and 1978 grids, and the 1979 grid instead carries 'STEVE WILSON, agriculture, Tompkinsville', who is the Stevie Joe Wilson of the back index. The one lead nobody has pulled: the 1976 volume carries a caption reading 'David Young, a sophomore from Bowling Green, enthusiastically cheers a play at the Tennessee Tech game', which is a named individual in a caption rather than a name in a crowd list. Whether that David Young is the 1978-79 administrative vice president is unestablished - a sophomore in 1975-76 would be in a fifth year by 1978-79 - and the 1979 index's man is 'Young, David Paul' with no hometown given. Someone with a spare fetch should pull that 1976 frame; if it shows one person it is at worst a FACE PROVED, PERSON NOT PROVED entry for the editor.

topic: THE archive.org BACK-INDEX PAGE NUMBERS POINT AT TEXT AS OFTEN AS AT PHOTOGRAPHS
note: Costing note, because it burned several fetches this run and will burn more. _talisman-index.json's page numbers come from each volume's own back index and are accurate as page numbers, but a Talisman back index references a person wherever their NAME occurs, including in running body copy. Three of the four pointers chased this run resolved to prose, not pictures. 'Wilson, Steve Alan ... 336' resolved to the fraternities feature where a Steve Wilson is quoted about Spring Sing. 'Young, David Paul 289' resolved to a sentence quoting the administrative vice president. 'Young, David Paul 277' in the 1977 volume resolved to a page carrying two fraternity group photographs, Alpha Gamma Rho and Alpha Kappa Psi, with no Young in either caption. Only 'Carlson, Georgiana Lynn 387' resolved to an actual class portrait. Before spending a fetch, check whether the same volume's printed class-grid list carries the person as 'FIRST M. SURNAME, Hometown'; that string is the reliable signal that a class portrait exists, and it is free to grep in the djvu text.

topic: GEORGE CARLSON AND GEORGIANA CARLSON ARE PROBABLY ONE PERSON, AND THE 1977 TREASURER'S RACE IS WHY
note: Not asserting it, but the evidence is now one-sided enough to be worth writing down where the next pass will see it. years.json holds them apart, and its own note on the George entry admits the doubt. What nobody had put side by side: years.json records GEORGIANA Carlson as the losing candidate for ASG treasurer in the April 1977 election, and the Herald of 12 Apr 1977 carries a letter from Tom Battle headed 'Wants GEORGE Carlson as Treasurer'. One election, one office, one fortnight, two spellings. Against that, the 1976, 1977 and 1978 Talisman back indexes - which list students who were never photographed, so absence is meaningful - contain no George Carlson at all, only 'Carlson, Georgiana Lynn' and 'Carlson, Gwen Axel'. The 1977 volume also puts a Carlson inside ASG that year in its own words: 'Christy Vogt, Bob Moore, Don Augenstein and Georgiana Carlson organize a rules and elections committee'. The remaining honest objection is that 'George' appears twice independently, in the Herald letter and in the ASG minutes of 22 Feb 1977, so it is not a single typist's slip. The document that would settle it is those minutes: if the nominee's name there is typed rather than handwritten, and if the same meeting seats a Georgiana, the two collapse into one.

topic: A CONCURRENT MERGE IS RUNNING AND IT PICKS CROPS UP OUT OF data/photos/ ON ITS OWN
note: Observed live this session, worth knowing before you drop a file in that directory. data/photos.json was rewritten at 16:51 by something other than this agent - I never opened it - and it had already absorbed two crops I had copied into data/photos/ minutes earlier, deriving the name from the filename slug rather than from my n6679.json entry. Bonnie Spinnogatti landed correctly. The Carlson crop landed as 'Georgiana Carlson', which is the right person for that face and is a name years.json already carries, so no harm was done - but it landed on the strength of the FILENAME, and my JSON entry for it carries FACE PROVED, PERSON NOT PROVED and was supposed to be refused and routed. The lesson for anyone filing an editor-flagged crop: the flag lives in n6679.json, the merge may only see the file, so NAME THE FILE AFTER WHOEVER IS ACTUALLY PICTURED and never after the officer you hope it is. The third crop of this session, 1978-79-david-young.jpg, was written after that merge ran and had not been absorbed as of 17:04; it is also editor-flagged and its filename does name the pictured man, so if it is auto-absorbed it will at least be absorbed onto the right face.
